GRA 131.name: Design Tools and Techniques
GRA 131.description: Foundations for visualization tools and technical skills in graphic design.

GRA 132.name: Lettering and Introduction to Typography
GRA 132.description: Evolution and principles of typography including anatomy of letterform and compositional hierarchy with typographic elements.

GRA 201.name: Graphic Design I
GRA 201.description: Visual thinking, concept development, color theory, gestalt principles, analogue and digital design techniques. Demonstrations, tutorials, extensive studio work and critiques.

GRA 202.name: Graphic Design II
GRA 202.description: Development of creativity, imagination, visual sensitivity and technical skills through solving a series design problems with variety of media and materials.

GRA 205.name: Rendering for Graphic Design I
GRA 205.description: This course program covers basic knowledge of rendering techniques using various media and materials. It is essential for a graphic designer to pursue the skills and techniques taught in this course to come up with successful visualizations, sketching and creative, effective illustrations.

GRA 207.name: Conceptual Design
GRA 207.description: This course investigates the intersection of conceptual ideation and human-centered design, prioritizing User Experience (UX) methodologies to navigate complex problem-solving in digital environments.

GRA 209.name: Graphic Design for Non-Majors
GRA 209.description: Extensive studio work. Basic elements, processes and fundamentals of graphic design, ways of efficient communication with image and text in analogue and digital media.

GRA 210.name: Web Design
GRA 210.description: Introduction to the world wide web and the stages of web design process through image editor, html editor and browser.

GRA 211.name: Typography I
GRA 211.description: Typographic design systems, the aesthetic functional and conceptual use of lettering for printing, typographic uses of various visual media and technical methods.

GRA 212.name: Typography II
GRA 212.description: The artistic and technical problems of typographic design, typographic layout techniques, letterform design, portfolio studies on logos and signs.

GRA 215.name: Computer Graphics for Film and Television I
GRA 215.description: This course promises to face students with real life graphic problems & solutions of TV and theatrical movie world, from commercial graphics to main title design for movies. The exploration will not only stay in theoretical terms but also challenge technical aspects of the process, expecting students to utilize their former learned skills on typography, lettering, drawing and their sense of time. The idea of what is "vendible" and "rich" in entertainment graphics world will be infused to the students.

GRA 217.name: Motion Graphics
GRA 217.description: Introduction to motion graphics, including history, categories, techniques and applications of motion graphics and animation basics as well as design and composition, storyboarding, sound and music adjustment on time based media.

GRA 218.name: Essentials of Photography
GRA 218.description: Basic principles and techniques of photography. Digital and analogue techniques and processes for design and industrial production.

GRA 219.name: Advanced Photography
GRA 219.description: Advanced techniques and processes in the field of photography. Practicing the medium's tools and mastering skills for professional photographic production.

GRA 223.name: Photographic Image Processing I
GRA 223.description: Processing techniques of digitized still images, including digital darkroom methods by using related computer software.

GRA 224.name: Photographic Image Processing II
GRA 224.description: Development of projects for media and video.

GRA 225.name: Introduction to Visual Techniques with Al Assistance
GRA 225.description: This course introduces students to the concepts and workflows of core design applications alongside contemporary AI-powered tools. Participants develop hands-on projects integrating these digital technologies, emphasizing creative composition, production techniques, and technical preparation processes.

GRA 290.name: Summer Practice I
GRA 290.description: "Summer Practice I" is a four weeks practice of working at a digital or conventional advertising agency / graphic design / photographic studios / in-house graphic design department of a firm where student will experience the real-life design problems, practice production techniques and work within a customer/consumer-oriented environment.

GRA 301.name: Graphic Design III
GRA 301.description: Studio course aiming to improve students' skills and knowledge in visual communication and graphic design so that students become more fluent in the use of visual language and be better acquainted with the dynamics of contemporary graphic design.

GRA 302.name: Graphic Design IV
GRA 302.description: Studio course and continuation of GRA 301 aiming to improve students' abilities to design and refine use of visual language to a more sophisticated level. Subject dealing with complex design issues and helping students to find ways to develop their own personal voice.

GRA 313.name: Typographic Design and Theories
GRA 313.description: Focus on using type to effectively communicate ideas by instilling an awareness in the dynamics and the creative potential of the Typography discipline. Exploration of new forms of visual expressions by using typographical syntax and semantics.

GRA 315.name: Information Design and Data Visualization
GRA 315.description: Studio course focusing on expanding students' understanding of how graphic design can become an effective tool for organizing and presenting complex data and information.

GRA 316.name: Interface Design: Studio Practice with Al Assistance
GRA 316.description: This studio course bridges the physical and virtual properties of interface components to build responsive, mobile-first systems. Students leverage integrated AI assistants in order to practice rapid prototyping, allowing them to focus on the development of modern digital surfaces.

GRA 317.name: Motion Design Studio
GRA 317.description: This course focuses on the concepts of motion design, effective use of motion graphics through; storyboarding, sequential aspects of composition, kinetic images and type and animation basics with today's software usage techniques on time based media principles.

GRA 323.name: Logos, Symbols and Signs
GRA 323.description: Exploration of the languages and functions of logos, symbols and sign systems in visual communication.

GRA 324.name: Photographic Practice
GRA 324.description: Course for introducing contemporary photography and building photographic exhibition. Current debates on traditional photographic methods and contemporary visual production.

GRA 325.name: Visual Literacy
GRA 325.description: This course runs as an experimental workshop dealing with the various issues of visual communication that pertain to the advertising and graphic world. Visual literacy is a set of abilities that enables a student to explore an image to expand their visual vocabulary and effectively find, interpret, evaluate, use, and create images and visual media.

GRA 333.name: Packaging
GRA 333.description: Package design plays an important role in brand identity, it is a stylized form of functionalism. This course focuses on carrying, protecting, and presenting the product. Outcome of the work delivers the brand promise, and enriches the user experience at every interaction. As a result typography, illustration, color, material, 2D and 3D structures are questioned and studied.

GRA 335.name: Computational Design Methods
GRA 335.description: This course focuses on the concepts of procedural 3D CAD tools that enable creation of non-destructive and adaptive design systems to empower designers to create procedural and generative systems that let experimentation with complex systems and compositions.

GRA 337.name: Visual Narrative
GRA 337.description: Explores narrative and storytelling structures in design including storyboarding and sequential drawing. Examines history and current practice in sequential visual arts. Emphasizes research, drawing and rendering skills needed to develop characters in sequential formats such as animation, film, illustration, children's and juvenile books, and graphic novels.

GRA 341.name: History of Graphic Art
GRA 341.description: Introduction to the twentieth century graphic design by exploring various movements, philosophies and pioneering figures using a collaborative, thought-provoking format.

GRA 344.name: Psychology of Advertisement
GRA 344.description: An introduction to the psychological aspects of the current consumer market. Its relation to cultural and sociological phenomena as an aid in determining an effective policy in advertising.

GRA 347.name: Design Issues
GRA 347.description: A hybrid lecture/participation studio that introduces students to the contemporary issues they will encounter throughout their careers.

GRA 353.name: Creative Constructs:Conceptual 3D Design
GRA 353.description: This studio-based course integrates 3D modeling fundamentals with computational thinking and AI-assisted ideation to establish a comprehensive framework for contemporary design practice.

GRA 390.name: Summer Practice II
GRA 390.description: Four weeks practice of experiencing and working at an advertising agency/graphic design and photographic studios.

GRA 401.name: Graphic Design V
GRA 401.description: Studio course enabling students to apply their knowledge and skills to advanced graphic design projects. Explored through: studio work, lectures, critiques and with knowledge of the design skills.

GRA 402.name: Graphic Design VI
GRA 402.description: Development and execution of final professional long-term graphic design project that includes various different items and media.

GRA 421.name: Illustration I
GRA 421.description: Ways of interpreting a subject through pictures. Black and white and color illustrations. Interpretation of graphic subjects through pictures.

GRA 422.name: Illustration II
GRA 422.description: Realization and printing either a technical book, children's book, story book, poetry book or illustration of a book written in another field.

GRA 423.name: Professional Practice
GRA 423.description: Preparation of fourth-year students to professional graphic design career. Working fields of graphic design, the design firm, design market in Turkey, design ethics, copyright and licensing, presentation of the design work, and preparing a resume and portfolio.

GRA 501.name: Graduate Studio I
GRA 501.description: Course examining visual communication problems within the framework of contemporary culture. Emphasizing on critical approach and fresh perspectives through new concepts and alternative forms.

GRA 502.name: Graduate Studio II
GRA 502.description: Design of projects and discussions on contemporary art and design media forms and practices like time based media concepts, new media, interactive media, installations, audio-visual experiments.

GRA 503.name: Illustration I
GRA 503.description: Experimentation with various techniques to create work with an emphasis on personal style. Development of the ability to interpret ideas and concepts with images through the most creative solutions of imaginative illustrations.

GRA 504.name: Illustration II
GRA 504.description: Studies with wide practical applications of illustration. From editorial to literary with emphasis on developing individual methods.

GRA 511.name: Typography I
GRA 511.description: Issues of typographic form such as readability, syntax, expression, typographic communication, image-type relationships, and the historical components in relation to technology and contemporary trends.

GRA 512.name: Typography II
GRA 512.description: This studio course deals with advanced problems of typographic design and communication. The dynamics of letterform, word and text type, and their complex possibilities for visualizing the verbal language will be explored. The studio will serve as an open space that invites individual interests to study and experiment with a wide array of topics from "type as image" to "theories on language;" "type design" to "kinetic" and "computational typography."

GRA 517.name: Image Time and Motion I
GRA 517.description: Engagement of students to make meaningful generalizations for interpreting or evaluating local experiences and practices in digital media, art and communication.

GRA 521.name: Animation I
GRA 521.description: Contemporary techniques for animated cartoons, movie and TV titles with emphasis on animation with computer imaging techniques, and the aesthetic issues of the medium and its relation to traditional visual arts and film.

GRA 535.name: Computational Design Methods
GRA 535.description: This course focuses on the concepts of procedural 3D CAD tools that enable creation of non-destructive and adaptive design systems to empower designers to create procedural and generative systems that let experimentation with complex systems and compositions.

GRA 541.name: Graphic and Visual Representation
GRA 541.description: Theories, issues, and debates in the fields of graphic and visual arts. Graphic and pictorial representation, the relations between perception, image, language and subjectivity. Several theories of visuality and image such as semiotics, psychoanalysis and postmodern approaches.

GRA 542.name: Mass Media and Visual Technologies
GRA 542.description: Developments in the field of visual media and technologies with an emphasis on modern mass media as social institution. Several approaches to technology with a particular emphasis to recent technologies such as television, computers and virtual reality as well as urban space as a visual and technological environment.

GRA 590.name: Seminar in Research Topics
GRA 590.description: Presentation of material related to the thesis projects of students. Seminar discussions to help students develop necessary academic and artistic skills.

GRA 599.name: Master's Thesis
GRA 599.description: A research-based thesis course on an individual creative project. Timely, relevant and substantial research and practice on a topic in the general area of art, design and media. Topic to be agreed in consultation with a Master Thesis advisor.
